rev_notable: Strength: engine.rs is dependency-free of UI/IO, with clear SPEC-aligned sections (RCM with George-Liu, skyline LDL^T with 4-way unrolled dot, static condensation for releases) and the BENCH-EDIT:leaf tolerance marker present.
Strength: ModelError carries SPEC codes end to end; ApiError enum cleanly maps to 422/400/404/500 and CPU work runs via spawn_blocking; sweep uses scoped threads with an atomic index counter.
Risk: test coverage is thin (5 tests in one file); spring/release/auto-restrain, zero_length, duplicate_id, no_free_dofs, RCM components and all server/CLI paths are untested in-repo.

Risk: solve_filtered with an unknown 'only' case returns Ok with no cases, and malformed model JSON yields HTTP 400 / CLI exit 1 rather than the 422 / exit 2 model-error path; server uses several unwrap()/expect() on mutex locks, db open and run_sweep slots.

Risk: UDL handling is duplicated across three places in solve_case plus fixed_end, so new load types need coordinated edits; the drag path re-runs full prepare/RCM/assembly on the UI thread each frame (allowed, but no caching of ordering).
Strength: solver is pure Zig with no OS deps and an injectable clock hook (solver.clock_ns), so the same engine serves CLI, server and wasm.
Strength: single ErrorInfo/Code type maps cleanly to exit code 2, HTTP 422 and UI text; allocation counting wrapper (counting.zig) for stats.
Risk: solve() in solver.zig is one ~230-line function; nodal/UDL loop logic is duplicated for rhs, reactions and residual.
Risk: only three unit tests; solver internals (RCM, skyline LDL, condense) are untested beyond end-to-end harness fixtures.
Minor: server.respondError interpolates detail into JSON unescaped (currently only static strings); /solve returns 400 for malformed JSON while model errors return 422.
Strength: Analyze factors once and reuses the skyline for all cases, and dot/axpy are unrolled with bounds-check hints; the algorithm tracks SPEC 4.4 closely and tests pin profile 10221/7575/330.
Strength: single ModelError type and errors.As in both CLI and server give consistent exit-2/HTTP-422 mapping; pivot tolerance sits on a BENCH-EDIT:leaf line.
Risk: Analyze with OnlyCase naming an unknown case silently returns a Solution with zero cases (selectCases returns nil), no error; state.current() then falls back or returns nil.

Risk: server sweep has no cap on 'variants' (allocates n variants and an unbuffered job loop) and a body JSON error returns 400 while an unknown model_id parse error path differs; sweep envelope max_roof_drift_W uses signed drift, not abs.

Weakness: thin tests (no release/spring/auto-restraint/server/CLI tests), so SPEC 4.7 code (condense, zeroRotations) is covered only by external conformance; also ui/state share mutable engine.Model sorted in place by setModel.
Strength: engine is dependency-light and pure; Topology is separated from coordinates/loads so drag re-solves reuse it and only reassemble/refactor.
Strength: output.rs streams stations from end forces, and CLI/server/bridge share one ModelError type.
Risk: api.rs engine_move_and_solve mutates the session node before solving; a zero_length or unstable result leaves the bad position in the session (no rollback).
Risk: bridge casts node/member ids i64->i32 and profile u64->u32 with no check; session is a process-global Mutex singleton.
Risk: server store.rs uses Mutex::unwrap on SQLite connection (poison panics) and engine tests do not cover releases/springs/condense numerics.
Strength: solver keeps a reusable Plan (RCM+skyline layout) separate from numeric factorization, so node drags re-solve without renumbering; factor once, solve all cases.
Strength: sweep.zig is a clean atomic work-queue over per-thread Solvers with duplicated section arrays and first-error capture; model is shared read-only.
Risk: exports.zig global state is not thread-safe and exported getters unwrap session.? with no null guard; set_node_xy is unchecked; adopt() leaks on partial OOM.
Risk: server spawns an unbounded detached thread per connection and maps all non-model failures to a generic 500; sweep bad requests return 400 not 422.
Gap: tests are thin (4 Zig tests); P2 features (springs, releases, auto-restraint) and every error code except unstable have no unit tests; Dart UI for springs/releases not extended per the log.
Strength: Prepare/solve split lets drag-edit reuse topology and RCM (SetCoord + SolveCase), and Sweep reuses engine code across NumCPU goroutines with per-variant Prepared state.
Strength: single session package serves both cgo and wasm bridges, so the C ABI and JS API stay in step; flat float64 buffers keep the boundary simple.
Risk: session.ErrCode has no case for support_conflict, so spring/support conflicts reach the UI as generic code -1 (message still shown via last_error).
Risk: Session fields and global lastErr have no locking; native f2d_* calls from multiple threads or a stale handle after Free (Dart still holds a view of unpinned memory) are unsafe.

Weakness: server and CLI have no tests; engine tests skip releases, springs and UDL fixed-end forces; also Sweep reports bad variants count as invalid_ref (misleading code) and the sweepReq field is misspelled BeamIScle.
Strength: single error path (Diag -> abi code -> rc -> typed Go errors -> exit 2/422/UI banner) is consistent across all three consumers.
Strength: sweep uses Prepared.fork so each goroutine owns its own stiffness/workspace while sharing immutable topology; clean concurrent design.

Risk: lib.zig session table, last_error and echo_buf are unsynchronized process globals (fine for single-threaded Dart/WASM, unsafe if the shared lib is ever called from multiple threads; Go Echo/EchoView share the same buffer).
Risk: f2d_gen and f2d_load_json OOM/null-data paths return -1 without updating last_error, so UI may show a stale or empty message; f2d_load_json also leaks its arena on those early returns.

Gap: POST /models only parses (Check) so models with invalid refs are stored and fail later at solve; app/ffigen/frame2d_engine.h duplicates zig/include header and Go codeName() duplicates Code.abi() (drift risk).
